messages.author: 4201c816d32af2ef
messages.subject: getting identifiers and other questions
parts:
Hi.

I am trying to process some exon data, both at 'exon' level and at
'transcript' level. There are a couple of things I don't know how to
do in aroma.affymetrix and maybe someone can direct me in the right
place.

Using Ken's use case and Elizabeth's descriptions, I am almost there.
As a first try, I've just taken 6 exon arrays from the affy web site
(3 heart, 3 brain).

Have fit plm for both merged and unmerged, as follows:

--------------
name <- "heart_brain"
chipType <- "HuEx-1_0-st-v2"

cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, chipType=chipType)
coreChipType <- paste(chipType, "core", sep=",")
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(coreChipType)
setCdf(cs, cdf)

qn <- QuantileNormalization(cs, typesToUpdate="pm")
csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose) #time required
plm.merge <- ExonRmaPlm(csN, mergeGroups=TRUE)
plm.nomerge <- ExonRmaPlm(csN, mergeGroups=FALSE)
--------------

To get the expression summaries, I can pull out the chip effects into
a table as:

[by transcript]
chp.merge<-getChipEffectSet(plm.merge)
d.merge<-t(matrix(unlist(readUnits(chp.merge)),nrow=6))
dim(d.merge)
####[1] 22010 6

[by exon]
chp.nomerge<-getChipEffectSet(plm.nomerge)
d.nomerge<-t(matrix(unlist(readUnits(chp.nomerge)),nrow=6))
dim(d.nomerge)
####[1] 233000 6

Q. I can easily get the ids of the 22010 transcripts from
'getUnitNames(cdf)', but how do I get the exon ids of the 233000.

I can get *all* (i.e. all 1432154) probe identifiers from:
cdfOrig <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType)
all.ids<-getUnitNames(cdfOrig)

Q2. Is there a way to get help with arguments of functions (methods)?
I find myself constantly entering the wrong arguments.

Q3. Now, if I wanted to play around with what exons belonged in what
transcripts (for example, a subset of even the 'core' set), how would
I go about this? And related ... how did Ken make his transcript ->
exon mapping?

Thanks,
Mark

messages.author: 9dda904b2c7a149c
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] getting identifiers and other questions
parts:
> Q. I can easily get the ids of the 22010 transcripts from
> 'getUnitNames(cdf)', but how do I get the exon ids of the 233000.
I think readCdfGroupNames() of affxparser will do what you want.

> Q2. Is there a way to get help with arguments of functions (methods)?
> I find myself constantly entering the wrong arguments.

If you use the HTML help that is generally the best way, if that
doesn't do the trick then try e.g.

args(getUnitNames.AffymetrixCdfFile)

so <method name>.<class>

> Q3. Now, if I wanted to play around with what exons belonged in what
> transcripts (for example, a subset of even the 'core' set), how would
> I go about this? And related ... how did Ken make his transcript ->
> exon mapping?

I'll have to think about your first question further (have to head off
to work now), but I can answer the second one. I got "metaprobeset"
files from the Affymetrix web site. It's one of the HuEx annotation
files - see

http://www.affymetrix.com/Auth/analysis/downloads/na20/exon/HuEx-1_0-st-v2.r2.dt1.hg18.zip

Then I took exon -> transcript mappings from those. I made a CDF
accordingly for core, extended and full sets of exons. If you are
going to use your subset of the core exons quite a lot then you may
want to do this and I have code that I can send you to do this. If
your subset is going to be changing then we need another approach.

Cheers,

Ken

> > Q. I can easily get the ids of the 22010 transcripts from
> > 'getUnitNames(cdf)', but how do I get the exon ids of the 233000.
>
> I think readCdfGroupNames() of affxparser will do what you want.

I couldn't get this to work for me. It just read all 1.4 million
ids. So, I wrote a function that untangles the list returned from
readUnits.ChipEffectSet. This is quite slow. Is there an easier/
faster way?


createExpressionTable<-function(chp.unm) {
x<-readUnits(chp.unm)
t.nm<-names(x)
x.ul<-unlist(x)
nc<-nbrOfArrays(chp.nomerge)
ex.data<-t(matrix(x.ul,nrow=nc)) # get exon intensities
rn<-NULL
for(i in 1:length(t.nm)) {
rn<-c(rn,paste(names(x)[i],names(x[[i]]),sep="."))
if( i %% 100 == 0 ) { print(i) }
}
rownames(ex.data)<-rn
colnames(ex.data)<-getNames(chp.unm)
ex.data
}

For example:

class(chp.nomerge)
####[1] "ExonChipEffectSet" "ChipEffectSet" "AffymetrixCelSet"
"AffymetrixFileSet"

I think I will stick with your CDF for the time being, but I would
like to know how to do this for the future .... e.g. to organize the
mapping to refseqs.

For example: in a case with overlapping refseqs, some exons may
"belong" to some refseqs but not others. For example, look at:
http://bioinf.wehi.edu.au/folders/mrobinson/hgt_genome_681f_d6aa40.gif
There are 11 distinct refseqs there for HFE. I'm not sure that an
exon array would be able to tell these apart very well anyways, but
you can see that not all exons belong to all 11 refseqs.
